title: Carne Asada Street Tacos with Onion, Coriander and Lime
summary: Skirt steak marinated in garlic, cumin, oregano and orange and lime juice is seared very hot, chopped and piled onto warm corn tortillas with a fresh tomato salsa.
equipment: large zip-lock bag or shallow dish
large cast-iron or heavy frying pan (or a barbecue)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
skirt or flank steak, patted dry
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Crush the garlic and whisk it with the cumin, oregano, cayenne, orange juice, lime juice, oil, 3/4 tsp salt and the pepper in the small bowl.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Rub the marinade all over the steak in the bag or dish and refrigerate for 1-4 hours. Don't leave it longer, or the citrus turns the surface mushy.

steps.title: Make the salsa
steps.text: Mix the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, coriander, lime juice and 1/8 tsp salt in the medium bowl and set aside.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Lift the steak out of the marinade, discard the marinade and pat the meat dry, since a wet surface steams instead of charring. Heat the oil in the pan over high heat until just smoking, or heat a barbecue to high. Sear the steak for 3-4 minutes per side, cutting it into 2-3 pieces to fit, until well charred and the thickest part reaches 63 °C.

steps.title: Rest and chop
steps.text: Rest the steak on the board for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice thinly against the grain and chop into 1 cm pieces. Cutting across the fibres keeps skirt steak tender.

steps.title: Warm the tortillas
steps.text: Warm the tortillas in the dry pan over medium-high heat for about 30 seconds each side, until soft and spotted, and stack them in the tea towel to stay warm.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Stack 2 tortillas per taco, top with the steak, chopped onion, coriander and salsa, and serve 3 tacos per person with lime wedges.

tips: Slicing with the grain is the commonest mistake; skirt steak turns chewy unless you cut across the fibres.
Get the pan really hot so the steak chars before it overcooks.
Doubling the tortillas, as street vendors do, stops the juices breaking through.
Warm tortillas just before serving; cold ones crack.
storage: Refrigerate the steak and salsa separately within 1 hour and use within 3 days. Reheat the steak once in a hot pan until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
